english: A: Why do you rejoice, woman? B: My son got up from his bed on the third(?) day. Didn't you know? A: I know. Does he eat now? B: He eats meat and drinks milk. His face is red again. Let us go to the house and drink mead. I praise the gods who protected your son. A: Be whole, dear.
uncertain: ḱósmi dinóy: read as 'on the third(?) day', ordinal unclear

english: A: Companion, a blade wounded my arm. B: Show me your arm. Who wounded you? A: A stranger. We fought at the river. The blade did not reach the bone. B: I smear fat on the arm and bind it. A: Will it heal quickly? B: You will grasp with it in summer. Now sit and wait(?). A: Companion, you are dear to me.
uncertain: kapyṓh₂ 'shall I grasp (again)' read as 'heal/use the arm'

english: A: Old man, tell me the words with which one binds the joint(?). B: Why do you want that? A: My brother's leg is broken, and in the village there is no one who knows them. B: 'Sinew to sinew I join, skin to skin I bind.' A: Should I sing it or speak it? B: Sing it; my grandfather sang it to me. A: I will not forget it.
uncertain: first sentence h₁yéh₂ h₂épesh₂ yunégti: 'which joins limb to limb'?

english: A: Old man, worms crawl in the flesh of my oxen. B: Did a wolf bite it? A: A wolf did not bite it; a thorn pierced its leg and the flesh rots. B: Cut that out and wash it with water and salt. Now pray against the worms. A: What shall I pray? B: Pray this: 'Worms great and few, die. Perkunos struck you with his stone.' Pray that three times in the evening. Then the ox will live for you.

A: Our sister-in-law, the white cow does not eat grass. B: Does she give milk? A: She gives little milk and groans at night. B: Is her udder swollen? A: It is swollen and hard. B: She has eaten bitter grass. Lead the cow around the house and do not let her lie down. A: Will she live? B: She will live, if the gods are friendly to us.

A: Mother, a snake bit my foot in the grass. B: Sit down and do not walk. Which foot did it bite? A: The left; it swells and burns. B: I cut bark and draw the poison out. A: Will I die? B: You will not die. The snake was small. Now drink this and be quiet.
uncertain: skéwHtim skélHoh₂ read as 'I cut the skin', not bark
